name: locateme
desc: Find your location using Apple's geolocation services
why: Queries Apple's location services from the command line, a rare view into how Wi-Fi and geolocation positioning work.

brief.what_it_is: LocateMe is a small command-line tool for macOS that asks Apple's geolocation services for the current machine's position. It takes no input file or data, only optional flags. It prints the result to the terminal in a default format, a long multiline format, a Google Map URL, or a custom template built from placeholders such as {LAT}, {LON}, {ALT}, {SPD}, {DIR}, {HAC}, {VAC}, {TIME} and {HOST}. The download is a single file, about 33k.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says it lets you "find your location (latitude, longitude, etc) using Apple's geolocation services" from the command line. The author also blogged about using it to find a lost computer.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the mechanism. The scout note says it queries Apple's location services, which the page does not describe in detail. The page only says that it outputs the current location and lists the fields it can report.

commands_seen.context: Usage synopsis printed by the tool's help text.
Run the script from the current directory when it is not copied onto the PATH.
Example of a custom output format. The documented output is lat=12.34567,lon=98.76543.
Example of XML-style custom output that includes altitude. The documented output is <lat>12.34567</lat><lon>98.76543</lon><alt>123</alt>.

brief.install_notes: Download the LocateMe file from the homepage (v0.2.1). Copy it to a directory on your PATH such as /usr/local/bin, or leave it in the current directory and run it as ./LocateMe. No other setup, accounts, runtimes or first-run steps are mentioned on the page.
brief.standout: It is a rare command-line window onto Apple's location services, which normally sit behind system apps and APIs. It has custom output templates, so it can feed scripts or XML directly.
brief.status: unknown. The latest version listed is v0.2.1 ("More forcibly quit app after location is found"), but the page shows no release date or last-updated date. The usage text still says Version: 0.2, which is a small inconsistency. Nothing on the page says the project is abandoned.
brief.caveats: The page is under the Mac OS X section, so it is presumably macOS-only, and it depends on Apple's location services. The page says nothing about macOS permission prompts, Location Services settings, or what happens when no fix is available. The page gives no source code or build steps, only a downloadable file. Licence: Public Domain, with the author willing to issue a release under MIT, BSD, GPL or other licences if needed.
